summary: Python raises one exception class per status; Go has one *APIError with StatusCode.
reason: Go code inspects errors with errors.As and a status field rather than a class hierarchy. TypeSafeAPIResponseValidationError maps to *ResponseValidationError; every other TypeSafe*Error with a status maps to *APIError. Python exposes retry_after_ms only on TypeSafeRateLimitError, so Go's APIError.RetryAfter() is compared for 429 responses only.

summary: A missing x-typesafe-request-id is None (or raises) in Python and "" in Go.
reason: Go accessors return the zero value instead of a sentinel or an exception, matching http.Header.Get.

summary: Omitted or null token counts are None in Python and 0 in Go.
reason: Usage.InputTokens and Usage.OutputTokens are plain ints by design (see the plan); the raw value stays available through RawJSON().

summary: Client-side misuse errors follow Go conventions.
reason: Go error strings start with "typesafe: ", begin in lower case, and end without a period. Messages are compared after removing those differences; Python's exception classes (TypeSafeError, pydantic ValidationError) are not compared. Messages that differ in substance are listed in the client-error-messages override.

summary: Some client-side messages name Go types or options instead of Python ones.
reason: Python's text refers to Python constructs (api_key=, dictionaries, pydantic validation); Go's names the Go equivalents. Both reject the input before any network I/O.

summary: Go rejects a state that does not encode to a JSON string, object, or array; Python sends it.
reason: Python's JSONContent type hint is not enforced at runtime, so 5, None, and True reach the server, which rejects them. Go validates state at encode time (a v1 design decision) and fails before any network I/O.

summary: A nil NoulCriteria outcome is omitted in Go; Python sends an explicit None as null.
reason: Go's NoulCriteria fields are plain any values, so nil cannot distinguish "absent" from "null". Both forms leave the outcome undescribed according to the OpenAPI schema (default null).

summary: Go never sends a caller-supplied Content-Type; Python forwards it on GET requests.
reason: Content-Type is a protected header in the Go SDK: it is application/json on requests with a body and absent otherwise (code review, P3).

summary: An invalid legend description reports answers.<n>.legend.<k>; Python appends pydantic's union member name (".str").
reason: The ".str" suffix is an artifact of how pydantic reports union validation errors and names no field. Go reports the offending field, as the plan specifies.

summary: Go rejects NaN and Infinity literals in a response as invalid JSON; Python parses them and then rejects the field.
reason: pydantic-core parses these non-standard literals, so Python reports the field holding one. They are not JSON (RFC 8259) and encoding/json cannot parse them, so Go reports the whole body as invalid and keeps it as raw text.

error.message: POST https://api.test/v1/systemone: 200 Invalid response data at ''.

summary: Go rejects NaN and infinities in request content; Python sends them as strings or null.
reason: Python 0.7.4 sends them as "NaN", "Infinity", and "-Infinity" in state and extra body, but as null inside question content. encoding/json rejects them, and silently turning a number into a string or null would change what the model sees, so Go fails before any network I/O as it did before.

summary: Token counts beyond the int range are a validation error in Go; Python accepts arbitrary integers.
reason: Usage fields are Go ints. Failing is safer than wrapping or truncating a count.

error.message: POST https://api.test/v1/systemone: 200 Invalid response data at 'usage.input_tokens'.

summary: A server delay at or beyond time.Duration's range (about 292 years) is treated as absent in Go.
reason: Go cannot represent the delay; ignoring it falls back to backoff, and the retry budget stops the call either way. Python keeps the float.

summary: Text that refers to an image the call was not given fails before sending in Go's SystemOne and SystemOneAs; Python sends the reference as plain text, as Go's CreateSystemOne does.
reason: A reference without its image is almost always a forgotten WithImages (Python: attach_assets), or an image behind an unexported field the SDK cannot see; sending the reference as text would silently drop the image. The JS SDK (@typesafe-ai/sdk 0.7.0) rejects such references the same way. CreateSystemOne keeps Python's behavior because proxies send it decoded requests, which hold no Image, so a reference in their text is the client's data.

summary: NewImage rejects empty data when the image is created; Python checks it when a call first sends the image.
reason: Go constructors return errors, so an invalid Image never exists. Python reads path-backed images lazily, which Go does not offer (see image-api).

error.message: image data is empty

summary: Go accepts a model entry whose release_date is absent or null and reports it as ""; Python 0.7.5 rejects the list.
reason: llama-server SystemOne servers (0.7.0, build 11669) return GET /v1/models entries without release_date, so a required field would make their model list unreadable. A present non-string release_date is still a validation error, as in Python. The OpenAPI spec still lists release_date as required; openapi_test.go records it in decoderTolerates. The fixture has no case without release_date.

summary: Go sends request bodies uncompressed; Python 0.7.5 compresses bodies of 1 KiB or more with zstd by default.
reason: The Go standard library has no zstd encoder and the module has no third-party dependencies. The API accepts uncompressed bodies. The generator disables compression so that request bodies stay comparable.

summary: Go offers NewImage, ImageFromBase64, and a per-call WithImages; Python also has path and Pillow constructors, an alias map (assets=), and the client-scoped attach_assets block.
reason: os.ReadFile plus NewImage reads a file without non-cancellable I/O inside a call, and Pillow has no Go counterpart. A call option is Go's scope for attaching images and cannot leak between goroutines; the parity cases map attach to WithImages. Aliases are text: strings.ReplaceAll(prompt, "<photo>", img.String()) does what assets= does, and proxies forward wire aliases through SystemOneRequest.Assets. Image is a value type, so an Image held by value in a struct still encodes as its reference.

summary: Request bodies are compared as parsed JSON, not bytes.
reason: Go's encoding/json sorts map keys (questions, choice criteria, raw questions, and the body when WithExtraBody is used) and escapes U+2028 and U+2029; Python preserves insertion order. The server parses JSON, so both are equivalent.

summary: Header names go out in Go's canonical form (X-Typesafe-Sdk) rather than Python's spelling (X-TypeSafe-SDK).
reason: HTTP header names are case-insensitive; net/http canonicalizes them. Headers are compared case-insensitively.

summary: User-Agent, X-TypeSafe-SDK, and X-TypeSafe-Runtime identify the Go SDK and runtime.
reason: They name the implementation (typesafe-sdk-go/<version>, go/<version>) and are excluded from comparison along with headers added by the HTTP library.

summary: Behavior with no Python counterpart is covered by Go tests, not this fixture.
reason: Context cancellation, per-attempt timeouts, credential redaction of transport errors, never-followed redirects (including malformed Location headers), and silent-by-default logging are Go-specific designs.
